figures.period: late-Edo Kyoto, Japan, about 1850
figures.name: Japanese samurai
figures.design: A samurai in full Edo-period armour (tosei-gusoku): a lacquered cuirass of horizontal plates in deep burgundy laced with ochre cord, broad layered shoulder guards, a skirt of plates, armoured sleeves and shin guards over dark hakama trousers, straw sandals. A rounded helmet with a flared neck guard and a small plain brass crest-plate at the front (no symbol on it), the face open and clean-shaven, the topknot hidden under the helmet. Two swords in their dark scabbards thrust through the sash at the left hip. Both hands hold a straight YARI spear upright in front of the body, its pale ash shaft as thick as a wrist, its bright steel blade above the helmet.
figures.lean: Full armour in Kyoto about 1850 is a military or ceremonial turn-out (the 1860s brought it back to the streets), not everyday dress; a deliberate adventuring choice.

figures.period: late-Edo Kyoto, Japan, about 1850
figures.name: Japanese spy
figures.design: A late-Edo Kyoto spy in ordinary rust-brown work clothes: a short jacket bound at the waist, narrow trousers wrapped at the shins, split-toe tabi and straw sandals. A charcoal headcloth tied over his hair leaves his face visible; an attentive, quiet expression. His RIGHT hand holds a short plain TANTO knife (bright steel, as broad as two fingers) point-down close beside his right thigh; his LEFT hand holds a compact coil of thick ochre rope against his waist. No symbols.
figures.lean: An imagined espionage character, not a documented Kyoto shinobi uniform; the earth colours are a production choice, not a claim about what spies wore.

figures.period: late-Edo Kyoto, Japan, about 1850
figures.name: Japanese onmyoji
figures.design: An onmyoji of the yin-yang way, associated with the Tsuchimikado household that still licensed diviners and made the almanac in Kyoto, in formal dress: a round-collared pale cream kariginu robe over plum sashinuki trousers gathered at the ankles, the wide sleeves resting close to the body, black lacquered shoes and a tall black eboshi hat. An older, clean-shaven, thoughtful face. His RIGHT hand holds a closed cream folding fan upright against his chest; his LEFT forearm supports a thick closed ALMANAC bound in a plain cream cover. No writing, diagrams or talismans visible.

figures.period: late-Edo Kyoto, Japan, about 1850
figures.name: Japanese sake merchant
figures.design: A Kyoto sake merchant: a plain brown-grey kimono with a short black haori jacket, a long dark-ochre maekake shop apron tied at the waist (no writing on it), white tabi socks and wooden geta clogs, the Edo townsman's shaved crown and small topknot. A broad friendly face. Both hands hold a big pale cream ceramic sake flask against the belly.

figures.period: late-Edo Kyoto, Japan, about 1850
figures.name: Japanese tea-house keeper
figures.design: The keeper of a Kyoto tea house, a middle-aged townswoman: a plain kimono in soft plum with a wide ochre obi sash tied at the back, a cream apron over it, white tabi socks and low geta clogs, her hair in a simple rounded bun held with one plain comb. A warm, capable face. Both hands hold a pale lacquered wooden tray with a cream teapot and two cups in front of her waist.

figures.period: late-Edo Kyoto, Japan, about 1850
figures.name: Ohara woman
figures.design: An Ohara-me, one of the village women who walked into Kyoto from Ohara to sell firewood: a dark brown work kimono with a pale cream pattern, white cloth arm and shin covers, straw sandals, a cream cloth over her hair, and a big round BUNDLE of pale firewood sticks balanced flat on top of her head, both hands raised to steady it. A weathered, attentive face.
holds: bundle of firewood on the head
figures.lean: Her occupation is documented; her exact dress follows later pictures and is a reconstruction.

figures.period: late-Edo Kyoto, Japan, about 1850
figures.name: Japanese town constable
figures.design: A doshin, a constable serving the Kyoto town magistrate, in a sober dark-ochre kimono, plain dark hakama trousers and a black haori jacket, with white tabi and straw sandals. Two sheathed swords sit at his left hip. A shaved crown, a small topknot and a watchful expression. His RIGHT hand holds a stout bright steel JITTE (a truncheon as thick as a thumb with one short side-hook) upright against his chest; his LEFT hand rests on the sword hilts. No official insignia or writing.

figures.period: mid-Qing Beijing, China, about 1770 (the Qianlong reign)
figures.name: Chinese bannerman
figures.design: A Manchu bannerman in a burgundy cloth-covered brigandine armour coat with small iron plates riveted inside and rows of bright brass rivet heads outside, black edging, split armoured skirts reaching below the knees, armoured shoulder pieces and sleeves, black boots. A rounded steel helmet with a tall stout spike finial and a close padded neck guard. A clean-shaven face. His RIGHT hand holds a broad curved steel DAO sabre upright beside his right shoulder; his LEFT hand holds its dark scabbard close against his hip. No plume, no symbols.

figures.period: mid-Qing Beijing, China, about 1770 (the Qianlong reign)
figures.name: Chinese wandering swordswoman
figures.design: A wandering swordswoman of the rivers and lakes (the xia of the storytellers): a practical fitted (not tight) jacket in moss green bound with a wide ochre sash, loose dark trousers tied at the ankle, soft black cloth shoes, her hair in a tight bun wrapped with a cream cloth, a broad bamboo hat lying flat against her back. A sharp, level gaze. Her RIGHT hand holds a straight JIAN sword (a bright steel blade two fingers wide) upright beside her shoulder; her LEFT hand holds its pale wooden scabbard down at her hip.
figures.lean: The wandering sword-hero is a figure of Qing fiction and storytelling, not of the Beijing record; she is the legend, dressed in plausible mid-Qing working clothes.

figures.period: mid-Qing Beijing, China, about 1770 (the Qianlong reign)
figures.name: Chinese Daoist priest
figures.design: An ordained Daoist ritual specialist of a Beijing temple, standing quietly in a plain deep-ochre robe over cream, the wide sleeves resting close to his body, white socks and black cloth shoes. His forehead is unshaven; his hair forms a compact topknot beneath a plain dark cap. A short grey beard. His RIGHT hand holds a broad blunt pale PEACH-WOOD RITUAL SWORD vertically against his chest; his LEFT hand holds a small bronze HANDBELL with a short handle, its open mouth downward, against his waist. No writing, talismans or symbols.
figures.lean: A ritual specialist of a real tradition; his game powers are an invention.

figures.period: mid-Qing Beijing, China, about 1770 (the Qianlong reign)
figures.name: Chinese silk merchant
figures.design: A Beijing silk merchant: a long brown-plum changshan gown to the ankles under a short black magua jacket with cloth buttons, a round black skullcap with a small red knot on top, the Qing man's shaved forehead and a long braided queue lying flat down his back, black cloth shoes. A lean, shrewd face with a thin moustache. Both hands hold a fat bolt of cream and ochre silk against his chest.

figures.period: mid-Qing Beijing, China, about 1770 (the Qianlong reign)
figures.name: Chinese mandarin official
figures.design: A Qing civil official of the fifth rank in his everyday court surcoat: a long plain black surcoat over a plum-brown robe showing at the hem and the horse-hoof cuffs, on its chest a square badge embroidered with a white pheasant among clouds (the fifth civil rank: a picture, no writing), a necklace of large round amber court beads, black boots, and the official's round hat with an upturned black brim, a red silk fringe over the crown and a clear crystal finial (the fifth rank's) on top, the long queue behind. A dignified, tired face with a neat moustache. Both hands clasped together in the sleeves in front of his waist.
figures.lean: Codex advised informal dress to avoid inventing insignia; this keeps the official's look but makes it ONE coherent rank (fifth civil: silver pheasant badge, crystal finial, court beads), since at table distance only the badge, beads and hat say 'official'.

figures.period: mid-Qing Beijing, China, about 1770 (the Qianlong reign)
figures.name: Chinese banner lady
figures.design: A woman of a prosperous Manchu banner household in Beijing about 1770: an ankle-length plum robe with a right-side fastening and restrained cream edging, a plain cream sleeveless vest, cream cloth shoes with modest thick soles over natural unbound feet. Her hair in a compact pinned bun with two small gold pins and one cream silk flower (no broad hair board). A composed expression. Both hands hold a closed pale folding fan against her waist.

figures.period: mid-Qing Beijing, China, about 1770 (the Qianlong reign)
figures.name: Chinese vegetable seller
figures.design: A market-gardener selling produce in Beijing: a faded ochre padded cotton jacket, dark brown trousers and black cloth shoes. His forehead is shaved and his queue is coiled beneath a cream headcloth. A weathered, attentive face. Both hands support one broad woven basket of green cabbages and orange persimmons against his waist, the vegetables nestled securely inside.

figures.period: Jaipur and Amber in Rajasthan, India, the 18th century
figures.name: Rajput warrior
figures.design: A Rajput warrior of the Amber court: a knee-length padded armour coat (a chilta of a thousand nails) in deep burgundy velvet studded all over with small brass studs, steel arm guards, a steel helmet with a short spike and a mail curtain over the neck worn over a burgundy turban cloth, a curled black moustache, tight cream trousers and pointed leather shoes. The RIGHT hand holds a curved TALWAR sword (a wide bright steel blade) upright in front of the right shoulder; the LEFT arm holds a round DHAL shield of dark-ochre hide with four bright brass bosses close in front of the left hip.

figures.period: Jaipur and Amber in Rajasthan, India, the 18th century
figures.name: Rajasthani court spy
figures.design: A harkara, a court messenger and intelligence runner: a plain cream knee-length cotton angarkha, cream trousers, a modest rust turban, a dark-ochre shawl folded close over his shoulders, leather sandals, a short dark beard and an attentive expression. His RIGHT hand holds a short KATAR push-dagger (a broad bright blade on an H-shaped grip) point-down close beside his thigh; his LEFT hand holds a closed bamboo message tube against his chest. No writing.

figures.period: Jaipur and Amber in Rajasthan, India, the 18th century
figures.name: Rajasthani court astronomer
figures.design: A learned jyotishi, an astronomer-astrologer of the Jaipur court in the age of its great observatory: a closed long cream jama robe, a moss-green shawl folded over his shoulders, a modest ochre turban, wooden sandals, a grey beard, a calm expression. Both hands support a big round bright BRASS ASTROLABE against his chest, with raised concentric rings and a broad central rotating rule in sturdy relief. No letters, numerals or inscriptions.

figures.period: Jaipur and Amber in Rajasthan, India, the 18th century
figures.name: Marwari merchant
figures.design: A Marwari merchant of the Jaipur bazaar: a big round ochre-and-burgundy pagri turban, a cream angarkha coat tied at the side, a white dhoti, pointed red leather slippers, a thick black moustache, a lean, careful face. Both hands hold a fat red cloth-bound account ledger (a bahi-khata, closed and tied with a cream cord, no writing showing) against his chest.

figures.period: Jaipur and Amber in Rajasthan, India, the 18th century
figures.name: Rajput noblewoman
figures.design: A thakurani, the lady of a Rajput noble house: a full ghagra skirt to the ankles in deep burgundy with a broad ochre border, hanging still, a fitted cream choli, a moss-green odhni veil drawn over her head and wrapped across the body, heavy plain gold bangles, a small nose ring and a small rounded gold borla ornament at her hair parting, bare feet with silver anklets. A composed, commanding face. Both hands hold a small bright brass oil lamp (unlit) in front of her waist.

figures.period: Jaipur and Amber in Rajasthan, India, the 18th century
figures.name: Rajasthani water carrier
figures.design: A village woman fetching water from the stepwell: a full ghagra skirt in rust and ochre block-print, a cream blouse, an ochre odhni veil over her head, plain silver bangles and anklets, bare feet. Two round bright BRASS water pots stacked one on the other balanced on a small cloth ring on top of her head, her right hand raised to steady them, her left hand at her side.
holds: two brass pots on the head
figures.lean: Her work is everyday; the exact jewellery and the stacked pots are a reconstruction, not a uniform.

figures.period: Jaipur and Amber in Rajasthan, India, the 18th century
figures.name: Rajasthani puppeteer
figures.design: A Rajasthani kathputli puppeteer: an ochre-red turban, a cream kurta, a white dhoti, a burgundy waist sash and plain sandals, a big curled moustache. Both hands cradle an inactive wooden PUPPET against his chest: a small turbaned man with a painted face, compact cloth arms and a long red skirt enclosing the lower body (kathputli have no legs), its arms resting against its skirt. No control bar, no strings.
holds: a wooden puppet in a red skirt

figures.period: the Viking Age in Scandinavia, about 950
figures.name: Norse shieldmaiden
figures.design: A Norse shieldmaiden: a knee-length mail byrnie over a burgundy wool tunic, a broad leather belt, wool trousers wrapped with leg-wraps, leather shoes; a plain rounded steel helmet with a short nose guard (NO horns, NO wings), her thick ochre-blond hair in one braid tucked into the collar. The RIGHT hand holds a broad leaf-bladed SPEAR upright, its pale ash shaft as thick as a wrist, its bright steel head above the helmet; the LEFT arm holds a big ROUND wooden shield painted in two plain halves of cream and burgundy with a bright steel boss, close in front of her body.
figures.lean: An exceptional woman warrior drawing on saga traditions and the woman buried with an elite weapon set in Birka grave Bj 581: her sex is securely established, her lived military role and how common women warriors were are still argued. This figure makes an explicit fantasy choice.

figures.period: the Viking Age in Scandinavia, about 950
figures.name: Norse outlaw
figures.design: A Norse outlaw, a man the law has put outside its protection: a short brown wool cloak folded close over a worn moss-green tunic, brown wool trousers, leg-wraps and leather shoes, a separate close-fitting wool hood over his head. A short reddish beard and a wary expression. His RIGHT hand holds a broad single-edged SEAX knife (a wide bright blade) point-down close beside his thigh; his LEFT hand holds a small iron hand-axe with a stout pale wooden haft close against his hip.

figures.period: the Viking Age in Scandinavia, about 950
figures.name: Norse volva
figures.design: A volva, a Norse seeress: a long cream linen underdress and a dark-burgundy wool gown, a short dark wool cloak folded close round her shoulders, a plain dark cap, a string of large amber and cream glass beads, a leather belt pouch and leather shoes. An older, attentive face. Both hands hold her tall stout dark iron ritual STAFF upright close to her body, taller than she is, its rounded bright copper-alloy finial above her head carrying shallow basket-like relief (solid, no open loops; no runes or carving).
holds: tall staff with a round metal head
figures.lean: Her look combines Viking-Age finds (the iron staffs from women's graves) with the later Icelandic saga accounts; her exact dress and her powers are reconstructed and invented.

figures.period: the Viking Age in Scandinavia, about 950
figures.name: Norse trader
figures.design: A Norse trader of the market towns: an ochre wool tunic with cream woven edging, a short brown wool cloak folded close and fastened with a bronze brooch, wool trousers, leather shoes, a soft wool cap, a silver arm ring, a full brown beard. Both hands hold an open shallow pale wooden case against his chest; inside lie two nested bright copper-alloy SCALE PANS, a folded balance beam and chunky weights, all flat and secure. A closed leather purse at his belt.

figures.period: the Viking Age in Scandinavia, about 950
figures.name: Norse farmwife
figures.design: A husfreyja, the mistress of a Norse farmstead: a long cream linen underdress, over it an apron-dress of moss-green wool held at the chest by two big oval bronze TORTOISE BROOCHES with a string of amber beads swagged between them, a bunch of iron keys and a small knife hanging at her belt, her hair under a plain cream linen cap. A strong, practical face. Both hands hold a pale wooden milk bucket with brass hoops in front of her.

figures.period: the Viking Age in Scandinavia, about 950
figures.name: Norse smith
figures.design: A Norse smith: a burgundy wool tunic with the sleeves rolled to his elbows, a plain brown leather apron, brown wool trousers, leg-wraps and leather shoes, short neatly kept hair and beard, a focused expression and a practical working build. His RIGHT hand holds a stout bright-headed iron HAMMER against his chest; his LEFT hand holds closed iron tongs close against his hip.

figures.period: the Viking Age in Scandinavia, about 950
figures.name: Norse jarl
figures.design: A jarl, a Norse chieftain at ease in his hall: a fine burgundy wool tunic with ochre woven bands at the collar and cuffs, a short cream fur-lined cloak folded close and pinned at the right shoulder with a gold brooch, wide wool trousers gathered below the knee, soft leather boots, a thick silver arm ring and a gold neck ring, a full grey-streaked beard, no helmet. His RIGHT hand holds a big pale DRINKING HORN with a bright brass rim close against his chest; his LEFT hand rests on the low lobed pommel of a sheathed sword.

figures.period: Mamluk-era Cairo and Damascus, the 14th century
figures.name: Mamluk cavalier
figures.design: A Mamluk faris, a cavalryman of the Sultan's household on foot: a knee-length coat of small steel lamellar plates over a mail shirt, an ochre silk surcoat with short sleeves over it, a rounded steel helmet with a short point, wrapped with a cream turban cloth, a mail neck curtain, burgundy trousers, soft red leather boots, a trimmed black beard. The RIGHT hand holds a flanged steel MACE upright in front of the right shoulder (a big bright head on a thick shaft); the LEFT arm holds a small round shield of cream cane wrapped with burgundy thread and a bright steel boss, close in front of the left hip. No writing on the shield or anywhere.
figures.lean: A real military class; this one is an adventurer on foot rather than a mounted trooper.

figures.period: Mamluk-era Cairo and Damascus, the 14th century
figures.name: Mamluk street thief
figures.design: A thief of the Cairo streets in ordinary working dress: a plain rust knee-length tunic over cream trousers, a broad ochre sash, soft brown leather shoes, a burgundy headwrap leaving his face open, a short dark beard, a quick, attentive expression. His RIGHT hand holds a plain short straight KNIFE (a bright blade) point-down close beside his thigh; his LEFT hand holds a small fat leather purse against his waist.
figures.lean: A fictional street thief, deliberately not the 'ayyarun brotherhoods (better attested for Iraq and Iran) and not the masked-dagger figure of Orientalist painting.

figures.period: Mamluk-era Cairo and Damascus, the 14th century
figures.name: Mamluk alchemist
figures.design: A scholar of alchemy in 14th-century Cairo, in the tradition al-Jildaki studied: a long cream robe, a moss-green outer robe resting close to his body, a round white turban, soft yellow leather slippers, a full grey beard. Both hands cradle a compact pale amber GLASS DISTILLATION VESSEL against his chest: a rounded lower flask fitted with a domed alembic head and a short thick side spout angled inward close to his body. No writing or symbols.

figures.period: Mamluk-era Cairo and Damascus, the 14th century
figures.name: Mamluk spice merchant
figures.design: A prosperous Cairo merchant of the Red Sea spice trade (a Karimi): an ochre-and-cream striped robe, a burgundy outer coat, a cream turban, soft red leather slippers, a well-kept dark beard and an attentive expression. Both hands hold a bright brass sample BOWL of dark peppercorns close against his waist. No writing or insignia.

figures.period: Mamluk-era Cairo and Damascus, the 14th century
figures.name: Mamluk water carrier
figures.design: A saqqa, one of the water carriers who brought Nile water through the Cairo streets: a knee-length cream cotton tunic with a rust sash, a small cream head-cloth, bare legs and plain sandals, a lean face with a short beard. A big fat brown leather WATERSKIN slung on his back over the left shoulder, its neck brought round under his right arm, both hands holding a bright brass drinking cup in front of his chest.

figures.period: Mamluk-era Cairo and Damascus, the 14th century
figures.name: Mamluk dallala
figures.design: A dallala, one of the women brokers who carried fine goods from house to house to sell to the women of Cairo: a long ochre robe, a big cream wrap (an izar) drawn over her head and around her body, a plum face veil across the lower face so her eyes show, red leather slippers. Both hands hold a big folded bundle of burgundy and cream cloth tied with a cord against her chest.

figures.period: Mamluk-era Cairo and Damascus, the 14th century
figures.name: Mamluk noblewoman
figures.design: A khatun, a lady of an emir's household, the kind who founded schools and fountains: a long full-sleeved burgundy silk robe with wide ochre bands at the cuffs, a cream silk over-robe open at the front, a tall rounded cap wrapped in a cream silk veil that falls to her shoulders, heavy plain gold earrings and bracelets, soft yellow slippers. A composed, shrewd face. Both hands hold a small bright brass casket in front of her waist.
figures.lean: Tall women's headgear is attested in Mamluk sources; its exact form here is a reconstruction.

figures.period: medieval Rus' (Novgorod and Kyiv), the 12th century
figures.name: Rus' druzhina warrior
figures.design: A warrior of a prince's druzhina in medieval Rus': a long mail shirt to the knees over a burgundy quilted tunic, a tall conical steel helmet with a little spire on top and a mail curtain round the neck and chin, leather boots, a full brown beard. The RIGHT hand holds a broad straight double-edged SWORD (a wide bright blade) upright in front of the right shoulder; the LEFT arm holds a tall almond-shaped (teardrop) wooden shield painted burgundy with a cream rim, close in front of the body. No symbols on it.

figures.period: medieval Rus' (Novgorod and Kyiv), the 12th century
figures.name: Rus' river raider
figures.design: A Novgorod river raider: a short brown wool cloak with a hood drawn up over his head, folded close over an ochre wool tunic, a plain belt, brown wool trousers and soft leather ankle shoes, a short red beard, a wary expression. His RIGHT hand holds a broad iron AXE with a pale wooden haft upright close against his shoulder; his LEFT hand holds a long broad knife point-down beside his thigh.
figures.lean: A fictional twelfth-century river raider, not a member of the later (14th-century) ushkuiniki.

figures.period: medieval Rus' (Novgorod and Kyiv), the 12th century
figures.name: Rus' village healer
figures.design: A village healer of twelfth-century Rus', a practical older woman in a long cream linen shift under a plain dark-ochre wool overdress with narrow red woven edging at the cuffs, a cream headcloth covering her hair, soft brown leather shoes. Both hands hold a small clay JAR and a compact tied BUNDLE of dried herbs against her chest. An attentive, composed expression.
figures.lean: A healer of an already Christian Rus'; her powers, if any, are a game invention.

figures.period: medieval Rus' (Novgorod and Kyiv), the 12th century
figures.name: Rus' fur merchant
figures.design: A Novgorod merchant of the fur trade: a rounded fur-edged cap, a restrained long burgundy outer coat to mid-calf belted with a cream sash, leather boots, a long full brown beard, a careful face. Both hands hold a thick bundle of dark brown sable pelts tied together against his chest.

figures.period: medieval Rus' (Novgorod and Kyiv), the 12th century
figures.name: Rus' princess
figures.design: A princess of a twelfth-century Rus' ruling house: a straight burgundy silk gown with ochre-gold woven bands at the collar, cuffs and hem, a cream mantle folded close over her shoulders, a rounded cloth cap and a cream veil over her hair, and two round gold KOLTY temple pendants hanging from short broad attachments at the sides of her headdress beside her cheeks (resting on the veil, not in her ears), a gold bead necklace at her collar. A young, serious face. Her hands clasped at her waist.

figures.period: medieval Rus' (Novgorod and Kyiv), the 12th century
figures.name: Rus' carpenter
figures.design: A Novgorod carpenter, a builder of log houses: a cream linen shirt belted with a plain woven sash, the sleeves rolled to the elbows, brown wool trousers, leg-wraps and soft brown leather shoes, neatly kept hair and beard, a practical, attentive expression. His RIGHT hand holds a broad iron CARPENTER'S AXE with a bright blade and a pale haft close against his shoulder; his LEFT hand holds a pale wooden mallet against his hip.

figures.period: medieval Rus' (Novgorod and Kyiv), the 12th century
figures.name: Rus' peasant woman
figures.design: A village woman of the Novgorod lands at harvest: a long cream linen shift under a plain burgundy wool overdress with narrow ochre woven edging at the cuffs, a cream headcloth over a plain cap, brown leather shoes, a sun-weathered, attentive face. Her RIGHT hand holds a bright iron SICKLE close in front of her waist, its curved blade turned inward; her LEFT arm holds a compact golden sheaf of rye against her body.

figures.period: Tenochtitlan, the Mexica (Aztec) capital, about 1500
figures.name: Mexica jaguar warrior
figures.design: A high-status Mexica jaguar warrior (ocelotl) of the military orders: a fitted jaguar-patterned war suit of close-laid featherwork over quilted cream cotton torso armour, ochre-gold with dark rosettes, rendered as smooth painted texture (no projecting feathers); a constructed jaguar-head helmet framing his visible face within its open jaws; plain sandals. His RIGHT hand holds a broad pale wooden MACUAHUITL with black obsidian blades set along both edges upright beside his shoulder; his LEFT arm holds a compact round woven CHIMALLI shield in plain cream and burgundy fields against his body.
figures.lean: The suit is a constructed featherwork garment, simplified for the miniature; the plumes and shield feathers are left off.

figures.period: Tenochtitlan, the Mexica (Aztec) capital, about 1500
figures.name: Mexica merchant spy
figures.design: A Mexica merchant who gathers news in foreign markets in disguise (a naualoztomecatl), in modest travelling dress: a short rough cream maguey-fibre mantle knotted at the shoulder and lying close to his body, a loincloth and plain travel sandals, his dark hair simply tied, an attentive expression. A small wrapped trade bundle sits on a compact pale wooden carrying frame on his back. His LEFT hand holds a stout pale walking STAFF close in front of him; his RIGHT hand holds a small black OBSIDIAN KNIFE with a pale handle point-down, half hidden beside his thigh.

figures.period: Tenochtitlan, the Mexica (Aztec) capital, about 1500
figures.name: Mexica day-count reader
figures.design: A tonalpouhqui, a reader of the sacred count of days who named children and chose good days: a long cream cotton cloak (tilmatli) knotted at the right shoulder with a broad burgundy border, over a loincloth, cream sandals, his hair long and tied back, a calm older face. Both hands hold a thick folded screenfold BOOK, closed, its painted pages hidden between plain dark wooden covers, in front of his chest.
figures.lean: A respected diviner of a real tradition, not a 'temple priest'; his game powers are an invention.

figures.period: Tenochtitlan, the Mexica (Aztec) capital, about 1500
figures.name: Pochtecatl merchant
figures.design: A pochteca, a long-distance merchant of Tenochtitlan's merchant guild: a knotted cream cotton cloak with an ochre border, a loincloth, sturdy cream sandals, a big pale wooden carrying frame (cacaxtli) on his back stacked with tied bundles of cloth and a round pot, a tump-line across his forehead, a broad weathered face. The RIGHT hand holds a tall pale black-tipped wooden walking STAFF (the merchants' staff) upright beside him.

figures.period: Tenochtitlan, the Mexica (Aztec) capital, about 1500
figures.name: Mexica market woman
figures.design: A woman selling in the great market of Tlatelolco: a cream cotton huipil blouse with a broad red-and-ochre woven band at the neck and hem, a wrapped ochre cueitl skirt to the calves, bare feet, her hair in two compact raised rolls at the forehead (a married Mexica woman's style). A round, shrewd face. Both hands hold a big round woven basket heaped with yellow maize cobs and red chillies in front of her.

figures.period: Tenochtitlan, the Mexica (Aztec) capital, about 1500
figures.name: Mexica noblewoman
figures.design: A cihuapilli, a noblewoman of Tenochtitlan: a fine cream huipil woven with burgundy and ochre bands over a straight wrapped cueitl skirt with a broad decorated lower border, a necklace and ear ornaments of dark olive-green stone, small plain gold bracelets, simple sandals, her hair in two compact raised rolls at the sides of her forehead (clearly hair). A composed expression. Both hands hold a rounded bunch of ochre and red flowers with short hidden stems against her chest. No blue-green colours.

figures.period: Tenochtitlan, the Mexica (Aztec) capital, about 1500
figures.name: Mexica featherworker
figures.design: An amantecatl, a featherworker of the craftsmen's quarter who made feather mosaics for the nobles: a plain cream cloak knotted at the shoulder over a loincloth, cream sandals, short hair, a careful, absorbed face. Both hands hold up in front of his chest a round flat FEATHER-MOSAIC disc (a shield face laid with feathers in a smooth flat pattern of red, ochre, gold and olive-moss green, the feathers lying flat like painted scales, none sticking out; no teal or cyan).

figures.period: late-Edo Kyoto, Japan, about 1850
